title: Consistent Hashing for Data Distribution
description: Learn how consistent hashing distributes keys across cache nodes while minimizing data movement when nodes join or leave the cluster.

data.text: Consistent hashing is a technique used in distributed caching to map keys to nodes in a way that minimizes reorganization when the cluster changes. Unlike traditional modular hashing (where adding a node remaps nearly all keys), consistent hashing only moves the keys for the affected node range.

With modular hashing, node = hash(key) % N. When N changes (a node joins or leaves), approximately N/(N+1) of all keys must be remapped — a costly operation that causes cache misses across the board. In a cache serving millions of requests per second, this is unacceptable.

data.title: The 1/N Rule
data.text: With modular hashing, adding or removing a node causes roughly 1/N of the keys to move. Consistent hashing reduces this to approximately 1/N of keys moving only for the affected range.

data.text: Real-world implementations use virtual nodes (vnodes) to improve distribution. Each physical node is mapped to multiple positions on the ring (e.g., 100-200 vnodes). This balances load even when nodes have different capacities and ensures more uniform key distribution than a single hash per node.

terms.definition: A logical copy of a physical node placed at multiple positions on the hash ring to improve distribution balance.
A circular namespace of hash values where nodes are placed and keys are routed to the next clockwise node.
The number of times each data item is replicated across different nodes for redundancy.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Consistent hashing maps nodes and keys to the same circular hash space
Keys route to the next node clockwise on the ring
Adding or removing a node only moves keys from the affected range
Virtual nodes (vnodes) ensure balanced distribution across physical nodes
data.takeaway: Consistent hashing is essential for production distributed caches because it minimizes disruption during cluster changes.
